verdicts.strongest_argument: Both underlying facts are published in the corpus with dates, and one of the finding's headline statistics is a tool artefact rather than a datum. The risk-factor changes, including the securitization language, were pushed to a public feed as an automated alert on 2026-05-29T11:36:09Z (docs/58c35b89...txt line 31-33) with the d-risk.ai/PHR/10-Q/2026-05-28 link, one day after the 10-Q was filed and one day after a print the market answered with +3.5%. The class action is published in the same feed on 2026-07-01T13:52:06Z with its specific allegation - overstated growth outlook 'while hiding weaker pharmaceutical marketing commitments in its Network Solutions segment' - and plaintiff-firm filings of that kind are press-released by construction. The Piper Sandler negative comment of 2026-05-28 is also in the feed. So this is not undisclosed information; it is disclosed information whose implication nobody in the capture has traced. On the '29,847 words against a 1,394-word average across 714 peers' comparison: that is not a signal about Phreesia. A 10-Q that restates its risk-factor section in full will always dwarf a peer set in which most filers incorporate the 10-K by reference and file only updates - the alert's own framing is '+2041.1% above peer average', which is the arithmetic signature of comparing unlike disclosure practices, not of unusual risk. Quoting it as evidence of risk weakens the claim. The tape gives the finding no help either: run_up_5d is +2.16% and run_up_20d +3.13% into the print, so there is no liquidity scare being priced, but equally the stock is 62.03% below its 52-week high, and the hunter honestly says as much - 'a good deal of it is in the price'. I credit that candour and I do not push this above the middle band, because the specific mechanism - a covenanted securitization funding a patient-financing book behaving as a liquidity constraint, interacting with softening Network Solutions pharma commitments - is genuinely drawn out nowhere in the capture, and the capture contains no sell-side note or preview at all to tell me whether the market has modelled it. That silence is a capture artefact and I have not converted it into either a concession or a refutation.

prior_publication.what_it_says: An automated public alert dated 2026-05-29 publishes the 10-Q's updated risk factors, including the added items, with the word-count comparison - so the disclosure diff was pushed to a public feed the day after filing.
Publishes the securities class action and its exact allegation about hidden weaker pharmaceutical marketing commitments in Network Solutions, two months before the print.
The 10-Q carrying the risk factors is a public SEC filing from 2026-05-28.
The opposite reading of the same financing arm - a $6bn payments opportunity meeting a profitability inflection - was also published, on 2026-06-10.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The 10-Q landed the day after the 2026-05-27 print, which moved +3.5% - the smallest-but-one reaction in an eight-event history whose median is 9.59%; the market did not mark the stock down on the risk-factor changes. Into this print the run-up is mildly positive (+2.16% 5d, +3.13% 20d) on 771,655 average shares, so nothing in the bars shows the liquidity constraint being priced now either - which cuts both ways and is why I sit mid-scale rather than high. The stock is already -62.03% from its 52-week high, so the broad de-rating (which includes the December and March -23%/-27% prints) is in the price. Baseline is sound (fits_cadence, 8 events).
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A quantified figure for the securitization program's size or its covenant thresholds against Phreesia's cash and Network Solutions revenue, drawn from the filing body rather than an automated word-count alert - that would move this into genuinely-undrawn territory and lower the number materially.

interactions: The claim and its own counter-source sit in the same document: docs/58c35b89...txt carries both the risk-factor alert and the bullish everyticker payments piece, so the corpus is internally two-sided on whether the financing arm is a covenant or an asset.
corpus_limits: PHR's capture has exactly one stored document and 29 retail messages across four months, with no news items, no sell-side preview and no consensus figure, so I cannot check whether the securitization or Network Solutions issues were in published models - the absence is a property of the capture's query set. I could not read the 10-Q body itself (only the third-party diff alert), so the covenant terms and the program's size are not verifiable inside the corpus. No options chain, so no implied move or skew.
